blinding_guess.why: The single listed element is declared in load_sia20d.launch via xacro.py (available in indigo), the xacro chain (sia20d.xacro -> sia20d_macro.xacro) resolves inside the package, and the checked-in generated sia20d.urdf matches the macro in link names, joint origins, axes and limits; I saw nothing wrong with the declaration itself, but I did not check the kinematic content against the physical robot.

notes: ROS 1 (indigo) support package with no compiled code; the only interface it defines is launch-file parameters. The parameter name is written relative ('robot_description') at load_sia20d.launch:2 and resolves to /robot_description when the launch file is included at the root namespace (the file is also included by test_sia20d.launch:2 and robot_state_visualize_sia20d.launch:25; test/launch_test.xml:33-35 includes it under ns 'load_sia20d'). The value is the xacro-expanded URDF of robot 'motoman_sia20d' (root link 'base_link', tip 'tool0', joints joint_s, joint_l, joint_e, joint_u, joint_r, joint_b, joint_t, fixed joint link_t-tool0), so the parameter has no message type, no header frame, and no msg definition hash; frame is left null because a URDF string defines its own link frames rather than carrying one frame. Units are not stated in the package (URDF convention would be metres/radians, but the code does not say so explicitly). QoS is null (ROS 1). The package also loads param controller_joint_names from config/joint_names_sia20d.yaml (robot_interface_streaming_sia20d.launch:16, robot_state_visualize_sia20d.launch:16) and sets use_gui (test_sia20d.launch:3); these are not packet elements. It includes motoman_driver launch files and starts robot_state_publisher, joint_state_publisher and rviz nodes from other packages, but names no other package's topic/service/param element, so references is empty. package.xml marks the package deprecated (to be replaced by motoman_sia_support).
